To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the renal excretion kinetics of famotidine and that of cimetidin are different, that the excretion of the former is inhibited by quinine, a classic inhibitor of organic cation transport, and the latter is inhibited by probenecid, a classical inhibitor of organic anion transport.

famotidine and other basic drugs are secreted by at least two renal tubular transport systems, one that is inhibited by cimetidine but unaffected by probenecid and the other that is inhibited by quinine but unaffected by cimetidine.

(1) famotidine and TEAB are excreted by the same renal transport system; (2) cimetidine is eliminated from the body by at least two transport systems; (3) famotidine is not eliminated by any of the transport systems used by cimetidine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the renal tubular handling of two H2-receptor blocking agents.
the multiple secretory systems involved in the renal elimination of famotidine and other basic drugs.
the competition between famidine and cimetidin in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cimetidine and famotidine are secreted by two separate renal tubular transport systems: (1) the organic cation system, and (2) a third system which is not affected by quinine and probenecid but inhibited by cimetidine.
famotidine and the cationic drugs, cimetidine and TEAB, are secreted by different renal tubular transport systems.

famotidine, like cimetidine, is eliminated in part by an organic cations transport system, but in addition, it is also eliminated by other renal tubular transport systems, which are different from those of cimetidine and which are not affected by quinine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cimetidine and famotidine are secreted by at least two renal transport systems, the first being an organic cation system and the second being an organic anion system.

cimetidine and famotidine are secreted by at least three renal transport systems: an organic cation system (which is inhibited by famotidine, quinine and high plasma levels of cimetidine), an organic anion system (which is affected by cimetidine, probenecid and high plasma levels) and a third system that is not affected by any of the drugs tested

famotidine and TEAB compete for a renal transport system that is different from that for cimetidine, PAH and quinine, and that probenecid may affect a minor fraction of the cimetidine secretion process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
famotidine and, to a lesser degree, cimetidine are secreted into the urine by more than one renal secretory system.
famotidine is secreted in the kidney by a mechanism different from that for cimetidine, and that cimetidine secretion is mediated by at least three different transport systems.
cimetidine and famotidine are secreted by at least three different renal transport systems.
